text:
The operator \(\vec P\) is the spin‑½ operator  

\[
\vec P=\frac{\hbar}{2}\,\vec\sigma ,\qquad 
\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\;\sigma_y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},
\;\sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.
\]

A direction \(\vec n\) in the \(x\!-\!z\) plane can be written as  

\[
\vec n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta),
\]

so that  

\[
\vec P\!\cdot\!\vec n
   =\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\sigma_x\sin\theta+\sigma_z\cos\theta\bigr)
   =\frac{\hbar}{2}
     \begin{pmatrix}
        \cos\theta & \sin\theta\\[2pt]
        \sin\theta & -\cos\theta
     \end{pmatrix}.
\]

We seek the eigenvector \(|\psi\rangle=(a,b)^T\) with eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\):

\[
\frac{\hbar}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a\\ b\end{pmatrix}
=\frac{\hbar}{2}
\begin{pmatrix}a\\ b\end{pmatrix}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\
\sin\theta & -\cos\theta
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}a\\ b\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}a\\ b\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Solving \((\cos\theta-1)a+\sin\theta\,b=0\) gives  

\[
b=\tan\frac{\theta}{2}\,a .
\]

Choosing the normalization \(|a|^2+|b|^2=1\) yields  

\[
a=\cos\frac{\theta}{2},\qquad b=\sin\frac{\theta}{2}.
\]

Thus the normalized eigenvector for eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\) is  

\[
|\psi\rangle=
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\\[2pt]
\sin\frac{\theta}{2}
\end{pmatrix},
\]

which is exactly option **(B)**.  
(Options containing \(\hbar\) are incorrect because eigenvectors are dimensionless spinors, and option (C) uses the full‑angle \(\theta\) and an unnecessary phase factor.)

**Answer: B**
